title: Etale closed-support bounds for the transported pro-etale exceptional functor
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow T$. Suppose $(W,T)$ satisfies the ordinary etale open-complement condition at $A$ with an integer $c\geq0$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound]. Write $i_e^!$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint to closed direct image, and let $Ri^!=
u_Z^*i_e^!R
u_{T,*}$ be the transported functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with $
u_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}	o S_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For integers $r\leq s$ the following two assertions hold separately.

1. If $B\in D_c^{[r,s]}(T,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals], there is a bounded constructible ordinary etale complex $B_e$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:
u_T^*B_e\cong B$, with $\mathcal H^t(B_e)=0$ for $t
otin[r,s]$. For any such witness there is a natural identification
$$Ri^!B\cong
u_Z^*i_e^!B_e,$$
and
$$Ri^!B\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z,A).$$
No finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed on $B$ in this assertion.
2. If $B\in D^b_c(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then every bounded constructible etale witness $B_e$ for $B$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$, meaning $\mathcal H^t(B_e\otimes_A^LM_e)=0$ for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf $M_e$ and $t
otin[r,s]$. The object $Ri^!B$ is bounded constructible and has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s+c+1]$, tested against every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf on $Z$, whether or not it comes from the etale site.

proof.text: Use finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to obtain a bounded constructible etale witness of each intrinsic bounded constructible input. Its interval equivalence, and degreewise homology isomorphisms for the witness, reflect each input cohomological interval. This uses no Tor hypothesis. Dependencies: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin].

source.place: Step 2, closed-support bounds; finite-ring comparison and the closed proper forget-supports identification.

proof.text: Expand the finite exceptional inverse image as inverse intrinsic realization, derived comparison direct image, ordinary exceptional adjoint, and intrinsic comparison. The derived realization unit cancels the realization and its inverse. The canonical unbounded comparison-adjunction unit is invertible at every bounded-below etale object, by isIso_derivedComparisonAdjunction_unit_app, the source-library form of site comparison. Restrict it to the full bounded constructible subcategory and whisker its inverse. For the closed immersion, rightDerivedLowerShriekIsoRightDerivedLowerStar identifies compact and ordinary direct image; transport the exceptional adjunction along it and apply rightAdjointUniq to the closed direct-image adjunction. This constructs a natural comparison on all bounded constructible inputs, which restricts to the interval subcategory. For any witness alpha, compose its component with the exceptional image of alpha inverse. Dependencies: [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], [lem-exc-closed-ambient].

proof.text: Apply etaleClosedOutput_bounds(a) to the witness and its reflected interval. Transfer intrinsic constructibility and the cohomological-support inclusion along the comparison from Step 2, using homology isomorphisms. This proves the first conjunct independently of Tor amplitude. Dependencies: [lem-pur-etale-closed-output-bounds].

source.place: Step 2, closed-support bounds; finite-ring comparison and the closed proper forget-supports identification.

proof.text: For every bounded constructible witness L, form its bounded-below object. Apply the reverse implication of comparison_torAmplitudeIn_iff. The exact-derived composition isomorphism and mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility identify the comparison object in that lemma with the given intrinsic witness. Compose representing isomorphisms with this identification and alpha to transfer the given Tor bound to the lemma premise. Thus every witness has the etale Tor interval. Apply etaleClosedOutput_bounds(b) to one witness and transport its intrinsic constructibility along the Step 2 comparison. For Tor, compose each representing isomorphism with that comparison, leaving the K-flat resolution and every arbitrary pro-etale module-sheaf test unchanged. Dependencies: [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval], [lem-pur-etale-closed-output-bounds].
